# Surah 88, image section 10: Göz: yere atılan bakış ve serbest bakış

## The section's prose (Turkish commentary)

İkinci ayetteki eğiklik önce gözdedir: {ar:الخشوع رميك ببصرك إلى الأرض, tr:el-huşûu remyüke bi-basarike ile'l-ard, gloss:huşu bakışını yere atmandır, source:"خ ش ع,B001"}; {ar:خشع ببصره إذا غضه, tr:haşaa bi-basarihî izâ ğaddah, gloss:gözünü indirdiğinde haşaa denir, source:"خ ش ع,B001"}. O gün yüz yukarı bakamaz, bakışı toprağa düşer. Kur'an bu bakışı birkaç sahnede gösterir. Mezarlardan çıkış için {ar:خُشَّعًا أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ, tr:huşşean ebsâruhum yahrucûne mine'l-ecdâs, gloss:gözleri eğik halde kabirlerden çıkarlar, source:54:7} denir. Sarsıntı günü için {ar:أَبْصَٰرُهَا خَٰشِعَةٌۭ, tr:ebsâruhâ hâşia, gloss:gözleri eğiktir, source:79:9} denir. Ateşe sunulan zalimler için ise eğiklik ile bakış bir arada anılır: {ar:يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِىٍّۢ, tr:yenzurûne min tarfin hafiyy, gloss:gizli bir göz ucuyla bakarlar, source:42:45}.

İki pınarın adı da gözdür: {ar:العين الناظرة لكل ذي بصر, tr:el-aynü'n-nâzıratü li-külli zî basar, gloss:gören her canlının bakan gözü, source:"ع ي ن,B001"}. Bu, ayetteki pınar anlamının yanında duyulur. On ikinci ayetteki pınarın suyu da göze açıktır: {ar:ماء معين أي ظاهر للعيون, tr:mâun maînun ey zâhirun li'l-uyûn, gloss:gözlere açık akan su, source:"ع ي ن,B006"}.

On yedinci ayet ise bugünün gözüne serbest bir bakış ister: {ar:أَفَلَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَى ٱلْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ, tr:e-fe-lâ yenzurûne ile'l-ibili keyfe hulikat, gloss:deveye bakmazlar mı nasıl yaratılmış, source:88:17}. Bakmak düşünerek bakmak demektir: {ar:تأمل الشيء ومعاينته, tr:teemmülü'ş-şey'i ve muâyenetüh, gloss:bir şeyi düşünerek göz önünde tutmak, source:"ن ظ ر,B001"}; {ar:تقليب البصر والبصيرة لإدراك الشيء ورؤيته, tr:taklîbü'l-basari ve'l-basîreti li-idrâki'ş-şey'i ve ru'yetih, gloss:bir şeyi kavrayıp görmek için gözü ve gönül gözünü çevirmek, source:"ن ظ ر,B001"}. Bakmanın bir de boş kalan biçimi vardır: {ar:ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون, tr:yenzurûne ileyke ve hum lâ yubsırûn, gloss:sana bakarlar ama görmezler, source:"ن ظ ر,B012"}. Ayetteki soru bu boşluğa karşı sorulur. Bakış dört yöne gönderilir: el altındaki deveye, yukarıya, karşıya ve aşağıya. Gök her yanıyla üstte olandır: {ar:السماء كل ما علاك فأظلك, tr:es-semâu küllü mâ alâke fe-ezallek, gloss:gök seni aşıp gölgeleyen her şeydir, source:"س م و,B004"}. Yer ise aşağıda kalıp göğün karşısında durandır. İkinci ayetteki bakış yere düşmüştü ve kalkamıyordu. On yedinci ayetten yirminci ayete kadar bakış her yöne serbestçe döner. Sure, o gün eğilecek gözün bugün henüz bakabildiğini hatırlatır.

Kur'an aynı soruyu başka yerlerde de sorar. Bir uyarıcıya ve toprak olduktan sonra diriltilmeye şaşanlara şöyle denir: {ar:أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا, tr:e-fe-lem yenzurû ile's-semâi fevkahum keyfe beneynâhâ, gloss:üstlerindeki göğe bakmadılar mı onu nasıl kurduk, source:50:6}. Başka bir soru bakışı habere bağlar: {ar:أَوَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا۟ فِى مَلَكُوتِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ, tr:e-ve-lem yenzurû fî melekûti's-semâvâti ve'l-ard, gloss:göklerin ve yerin hükümranlığına bakmadılar mı, source:7:185}. Aynı ayet şöyle biter: {ar:فَبِأَىِّ حَدِيثٍۭ بَعْدَهُۥ يُؤْمِنُونَ, tr:fe-bi-eyyi hadîsin ba'dehû yu'minûn, gloss:bundan sonra hangi habere inanacaklar, source:7:185}. Dünyaya bakmak ile ilk ayetteki haber burada birleşir. Bakış diriltmeye de bağlanır: {ar:قُلْ سِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ بَدَأَ ٱلْخَلْقَ ۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْءَاخِرَةَ, tr:kul sîrû fi'l-ardi fenzurû keyfe bedee'l-halka summallâhu yunşiu'n-neş'ete'l-âhira, gloss:de ki yeryüzünde gezin de yaratmayı nasıl başlattığına bakın; sonra Allah son yaratılışı yapacak, source:29:20}; {ar:فَٱنظُرْ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِ رَحْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْىِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ, tr:fenzur ilâ âsâri rahmetillâhi keyfe yuhyi'l-arda ba'de mevtihâ, gloss:Allah'ın rahmetinin izlerine bak; yeri ölümünden sonra nasıl diriltir, source:30:50}. Bahçede ise bakış yükseltilmiş yerlerden yapılır: {ar:عَلَى ٱلْأَرَآئِكِ يَنظُرُونَ, tr:ale'l-erâiki yenzurûn, gloss:koltuklar üstünde bakarlar, source:83:23}. Bakışın varacağı en uç yer de şudur: {ar:إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌۭ, tr:ilâ rabbihâ nâzıra, gloss:Rablerine bakan, source:75:23}.

const body = `strong\t54:7\tscene+root\tThe source section's root خ ش ع and its gloss of a gaze lowered to earth recur in خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ: people emerge from graves with humbled eyes, the same bodily scene the section draws from.
strong\t79:9\tscene+root\tThe section names خ ش ع for eyes cast down; here أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives that posture at the Day of Resurrection, after the preceding verse's trembling faces.
medium\t79:8\tneighbour+scene\tAfter this verse's trembling hearts, 79:9 says the eyes are humbled; the cited ayah adds the inner dread surrounding the downcast gaze.
strong\t42:45\tscene+root\tThe section directly cites this image: wrongdoers shown to the fire look from a hidden corner of the eye, يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ. It makes the gaze itself a sign of humiliation.
strong\t68:43\tscene+root\tThe section's خ ش ع eye posture appears as خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ, with disgrace overtaking those who cannot raise their gaze.
medium\t68:42\tneighbour+scene\tThis verse calls them to prostrate and says they cannot; the following 68:43 contributes the humbled eyes, linking failed bodily submission to the gaze's humiliation.
strong\t70:44\tscene+root\tThe source section's root خ ش ع is applied directly to eyes here: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ, as disgrace overtakes those facing judgment.
medium\t70:43\tneighbour+scene\tThis verse has people rushing toward the caller; 70:44 then supplies the humbled eyes and disgrace, continuing the resurrection scene of the section.
contrast\t24:30\troot+contrast\tThe source section's lowered gaze is forced by the coming Day; here يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ commands men to lower their eyes now, making deliberate restraint a present counterpart.
contrast\t24:31\troot+contrast\tThe same root-and-eye detail appears in يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِنَّ: women are told to lower their gaze by choice, a present boundary beside the section's humbled gaze in judgment.
contrast\t14:42\tscene+contrast\tThe section's downcast gaze meets its reversal in تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ: on the promised Day eyes stare in terror rather than falling toward earth.
medium\t14:43\tneighbour+scene\tAfter 14:42 says eyes stare, this verse adds heads lifted and eyelids not returning; it sharpens the fixed, terrified gaze that contrasts with the section's lowered one.
contrast\t21:97\tscene+contrast\tThe section shows eyes lowered on the Day; here the disbelievers' eyes are fixed wide in fear, شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, an opposite posture.
strong\t40:19\troot+scene+contrast\tThe section's hidden eye-corner glance is reversed by God's knowledge of خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: a stealthy look is hidden from people but exposed to divine sight.
strong\t7:198\troot+theme\tThe source section quotes the dictionary example ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون; this ayah says idols seem to look at the observer but do not see, directly distinguishing looking from perceiving.
strong\t10:43\troot+theme\tThe source section contrasts reflective النظر with merely looking; this verse says some look at the Prophet but remain blind, so sight alone does not become understanding.
strong\t7:179\ttheme+contrast\tThe section asks for a seeing that considers creation; here people have eyes لا يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا and hearts that do not understand, a direct boundary between eyes and perception.
medium\t6:25\ttheme+contrast\tThe section's question asks people to read signs by looking; this verse says some see every sign yet will not believe, showing how an open gaze can remain unresponsive.
medium\t18:101\troot+theme\tThe section's root ع ي ن names the eye and its gaze; here eyes are covered from God's reminder, a concrete case where physical eyes fail to receive what is shown.
medium\t22:46\ttheme+contrast\tThe section's thoughtful looking joins eye and insight; this verse says blindness is in hearts, not the eyes, distinguishing bodily sight from the perception its question demands.
contrast\t20:124\ttheme+contrast\tThe section says today's eyes can still look before the Day when they are humbled; this verse reverses that present ability by saying the one who turns from remembrance will be raised blind.
strong\t50:22\ttheme+contrast\tThe section contrasts today's available gaze with the coming reckoning; here the veil is removed and sight becomes sharp, revealing what a person had failed to see.
contrast\t53:17\tscene+contrast\tThe section's gaze can turn freely across the world; here the Prophet's sight neither swerved nor exceeded, مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى, a stated limit on a particular vision.
strong\t53:18\tneighbour+scene\tAfter 53:17 defines the gaze as neither diverted nor excessive, this verse says it saw the greatest signs of its Lord; the cited ayah gives the object of that disciplined sight.
strong\t75:23\tscene+root\tThe source section explicitly names this as the farthest destination of النظر: faces on that Day look toward their Lord, إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ.
strong\t83:23\tscene+root\tThe section cites this raised, free gaze: people reclining on couches look around, عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ, a paradise counterpart to eyes cast down.
medium\t83:35\troot+scene+contrast\tThe source section's couch-side looking recurs here for the righteous; set beside the section's fire-facing hidden glance, the same verb marks opposite destinies.
contrast\t7:143\tscene+contrast\tThe section names the Lord-directed gaze of 75:23; here Moses asks to see God and is told he will not see Him, while the mountain crumbles at the manifestation. It marks a boundary around the image of looking toward God.
contrast\t6:103\troot+contrast\tThe source section cites a gaze directed toward the Lord; this ayah sets a boundary by saying eyes do not encompass Him, clarifying that directed sight is not exhaustive grasp.
